summary: This bill awards a single Congressional Gold Medal collectively to the women who served in the U.S. Army and Navy Nurse Corps during World War II, directing the Treasury Secretary to design and strike the medal for presentation by the Speaker of the House and Senate President pro tempore, after which it is transferred to the Smithsonian Institution.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes use of the US Mint Public Enterprise Fund to cover medal production costs, with duplicate bronze medals sold to recoup expenses. This represents negligible, one-time administrative spending with no expansion of ongoing government programs or budgets.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue policy.
While the bill honors historical military nurses, it does not address any aspect of the current healthcare system, coverage, or delivery models.
No provisions related to firearms, regulations, or gun rights.
No provisions related to immigration policy, borders, or pathways.
No provisions related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill honors WWII military nurses but does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense spending levels.
No provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
No provisions related to welfare programs or social safety net policies.
No provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
No provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
No provisions related to sentencing, policing, or criminal justice reform.
No provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The minor costs associated with medal production are offset by sales of duplicates and have no meaningful impact on deficit or debt policy.
No provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
No provisions related to foreign aid.
No provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
No provisions related to technology regulation or data privacy.
No provisions related to labor rights or unions.
No provisions related to religious exemptions or anti-discrimination laws.
